To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) machine learning algorithms using limited data from experiments can be used to predict new materials in a high dimensional design space that considers composition, heat treatment and processing, 2) this is enabled by a physics informed feature engineering process that combines previously engineered composition features with newly engineered heat treatments features, and 3) the new heat treatment features are obtained by pre processing the data using mathematical relationships that describe the thermodynamics of precipitation in alloys, and result in greatly improved performance.

machine learning algorithms trained on relatively small amounts of data from physical experiments can be used to predict new alloys and their processing, provided a physics informed feature engineering strategy is used to pre process the experimental data.
Machine learning using limited amounts of data can be used to predict new shape-memory-alloys in a high-dimensional alloy design space.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of machine learning for alloy design and development.
using physics informed feature engineering to enable ML to predict the properties of new alloys with limited amounts of physical data, and is demonstrated here with a shape memory alloy example.
the application of machine learning techniques to the problem of alloy design.

a combination of physics informed feature engineering and machine learning can be used to make accurate predictions for new alloys and post processing conditions with a limited amount of data.
machine learning using limited data and physics informed features can predict new materials.

the use of physics informed feature engineering to pre-process data is shown to be an effective approach for using machine learning to make predictions of materials performance in a high dimensional design space with limited experimental data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the physics informed feature engineering (PIFE) approach can be used to enable machine learning to make predictions of materials properties in the absence of large amounts of data, and that this approach has the potential to be broadly applicable to other materials design problems.
the physics informed feature engineering enables machine learning to work with limited data for alloy design, which is an important step toward the goal of using ML for alloy design.
a physics informed feature engineering strategy is shown to be an effective approach to use ML for alloy design.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a physics-informed machine learning approach can be used to predict new alloys in a high-dimensional design space with limited data, and the key to this approach is a featured engineering that combines physics-informed features with ML features.
the combination of physics informed feature engineering with the application of machine learning to materials science data can be a highly effective approach to materials design.
